newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha confirms will call election.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha confirms will call election.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha confirmed on Wednesday he would dissolve parliament and call elections for the end of June, although most other political parties have said they may boycott the poll.

The elections are seen as vital to restore stability and calm in Albania after the violent riots of February and March which followed the collapse of pyramid investment schemes. But a boycott of the vote by the other parties would make a mockery of the elections, Western diplomats say.

"Today in the afternoon I will decree the election day and will dissolve the parliament, which you elected (last year) with your free vote, the martyr parliament of the rebellion and we will elect a more powerful and wiser parliament," Berisha told a crowd of several hundred people in this town some 50 km (30 miles) from Tirana. He said the vote would take place on June 29.

Albania's other political parties said they might boycott the vote after Berisha's Democratic Party on Tuesday forced through parliament an election law which the other parties said favours the Democrats.

The passing of an election law was part of a political contract signed by the Democrats and the other eight parties of a Government of National Reconciliation, set up amid the March rioting to help stop the violence.

But the other parties, led by the second-largest party in parliament, the Socialists, wanted the election law to be presented by the government and not the Democrats alone. They also opposed a division of seats to be decided by proportional and majority voting.
